keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «기회비용은 포기한 가장 좋은 선택의 가치이다(개념)» 와 «기회비용을 생각하면 정말 포기하는 것이 무엇인지 알아차리고 더 현명하게 선택할 수 있다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the concept (opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up) and the conclusion (thinking about opportunity cost helps us notice what we give up and make wiser choices). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Opportunity cost, the hidden price of every choice

sum.pre: Our wants are almost unlimited, but our time and money are

words: The basic problem of economics is scarcity
a situation where there is not enough of something
Economists call it opportunity cost, which means the value of the best option you give up.
our time, money, and resources are limited
only a certain amount, not endless
the value of the best option you give up
one of the things you can choose
Interestingly, opportunity cost is not always measured in money.

Behavioral economists have shown that emotions, habits, and the way choices are presented can strongly affect our decisions.

qs.q: Why does every choice have a cost?
opts: Because our time, money, and resources are limited
Because every store raises its prices
Because economists make our choices for us
evs: Because of scarcity, every choice has a cost.
When a government spends more on roads, it may have less money for schools or hospitals.
Behavioral economists have shown that emotions, habits, and the way choices are presented can strongly affect our decisions.
You could go to a movie with friends, study for a test, or earn money at a part-time job.
why: 본문에 «Because of scarcity, every choice has a cost» 라고 나와요. 원하는 것은 많은데 시간과 돈 같은 자원은 한정되어 있어서(희소성), 하나를 고르면 다른 것을 포기해야 해요.
The text says that because of scarcity, every choice has a cost. Our resources are limited, so choosing one thing means giving up another.

qs.q: In the text, what does "opportunity cost" mean?
opts: The value of the best option you give up when you choose
The price printed on a movie ticket
The money a government spends on roads
evs: Economists call it opportunity cost, which means the value of the best option you give up.
If you choose the movie, your opportunity cost might be the money you could have earned at work.
This idea also explains decisions made by countries and companies.
why: 기회비용은 «포기한 가장 좋은 선택의 가치» 라고 정의하고, 영화를 고르면 일해서 벌 수 있었던 돈이 기회비용이 된다는 예를 들어요.
Opportunity cost is defined as the value of the best option you give up. For example, if you choose the movie, the cost might be the money you could have earned.

qs.q: Why do many people stay in a boring movie, according to the text?
qs.qko: 글에 따르면, 많은 사람이 지루한 영화를 끝까지 보는 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Emotions and habits affect decisions, so they stay just because they already paid
The movie usually gets better near the end
Leaving the theater early costs extra money
evs: Behavioral economists have shown that emotions, habits, and the way choices are presented can strongly affect our decisions.
For example, many people stay in a boring movie simply because they already paid for the ticket, even though that money is gone either way.
If you choose the movie, your opportunity cost might be the money you could have earned at work.
Even something that seems free has an opportunity cost, because it still takes your time.
why: 감정과 습관이 결정에 큰 영향을 준다고 하고, 그 예로 이미 표값을 냈다는 이유만으로 지루한 영화를 끝까지 본다고 해요. 그 돈은 어차피 돌아오지 않는데도요.
Emotions and habits can strongly affect decisions. For example, people stay in a boring movie because they already paid, even though that money is gone either way.

ends: What is a sunk cost, and why is it so hard to ignore?
매몰 비용은 무엇이고, 왜 무시하기 어려울까?
How does a government decide what to spend money on?
정부는 돈을 어디에 쓸지 어떻게 정할까?
